verdict.rationale: Oyster's first-party docs describe outbound webhooks that push platform events to a consumer endpoint. Deliveries carry a bearer-token secret you supply, are retried up to 9 times over about 48 hours, and use named events (e.g. expenses.expense_approved) so consumers can filter. Missing for 10: an explicit registration/subscription procedure (only implied by 'the secret you provide here'), a full event catalog, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks are a way of receiving information from the Oyster platform by getting it "pushed" to you, as opposed to continually making requests ("polling")
We will include the secret you provide here as an Authorization header (bearer token) in all webhooks we send to you, to prove they've come from the Oyster platform.
Oyster will automatically retry webhook delivery up to 9 total attempts over approximately 48 hours
This will allow you to filter for only the events you care about.
